subject: BrightLeaf DPA: subprocessor & analytics export language — Product/Security review

Subject: BrightLeaf DPA: subprocessor & analytics export language — Product/Security review

Hi team —

BrightLeaf sent back a DPA with three asks that we need Product + Security guidance on before we can move to signature: attached PDF has their markups. High-level: 1) they want an explicit analytics-export carveout allowing aggregated telemetry to be exported to BrightLeaf for model performance dashboards; 2) they request our ability to add a monitoring subprocessor (LogSight Inc.) to the runtime stack and want the right to require that subprocessor be listed as a permitted subproc in the contract; 3) they want the clause that forbids any use of customer data for model training to include an exception for “safe anonymized telemetry used solely for service improvement.”

As a reminder, the commercial team needs a final sign-off by EOD Friday PDT to keep the Q2 close.

Can you please:
- Olga: confirm whether the analytics-export carveout can be scoped (metrics-only, no raw prompts) and what product guardrails you’d require (retention window, pseudonymization).
- Karthik: advise on whether LogSight can be accepted (they have a managed SIEM with DB access), and what evidence we need (SOC2 + vendor encryption at rest).
- Jasmine: flag any product rollout constraints if we need to add subproc monitoring earlier than our normal approval cycle.

Attachment: BrightLeaf_DPA_redlines_20270518.pdf (pdf, 124 KB)

Thanks —
Marcus

Subject: Re: BrightLeaf DPA: subprocessor & analytics export language — Product/Security review

Thanks Marcus — quick responses inline.

1) Analytics export carveout: product OK with a metrics-only export if we explicitly limit export to aggregated counters, histograms, and anonymized latency/prompt-size buckets. No raw prompts, no embeddings, and no per-user session identifiers. Required guardrails: a hard retention window (30 days) for telemetry kept on our side, and pseudonymization for any field that could be tied back to an end user. We should also limit export cadence to daily batches and require BrightLeaf to store only aggregated data.

Proposed language sketch (high level): "Provider may export aggregated, non-identifying telemetry metrics to Customer for the sole purpose of product analytics and model performance monitoring. Exported data must not include raw customer prompts, embeddings, or identifiers; retention on Provider side shall not exceed 30 days."

2) Subprocessor: adding a monitoring vendor as a runtime subprocessor is acceptable in principle, but any vendor that receives runtime payload (even telemetry) must be bound by equivalent contractual restrictions (no model training, encryption at rest, SOC2 Type II). We should also insist on a notification + 30-day objection window rather than permissive unilateral addition.

3) Training carveout language: we cannot accept a broadly scoped exception that allows BrightLeaf to use anonymized data for model training. If they want a limited exception for telemetry, it must be strictly defined (metrics-only, aggregated, and only after additional anonymization that prevents reconstruction of prompts). Prefer to keep the "no training" stance and allow a very narrow analytics-export as above.

If Legal wants a specific redline, I can draft the revised paragraph this afternoon.

- Olga
Head of Product, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: BrightLeaf DPA: subprocessor & analytics export language — Product/Security review

Appreciate the context. Security position: we should be conservative but pragmatic to avoid killing the deal. Specifics:

- LogSight: before approval we need a vendor package: SOC2 Type II report within the last 12 months, confirmation of encryption at rest (AES-256 or equivalent), and proof of customer-segregated storage or strong tenancy isolation for log data. If BrightLeaf cannot provide these, we should require us (Provider) to proxy telemetry to LogSight rather than handing over raw data.

- Subprocessor addition process: we cannot accept language that allows BrightLeaf to unilaterally require subprocessor additions. Our standard is 30-day notice plus right to object for legitimate security reasons. We can add a clause: "Customer may propose the use of a named third-party monitoring vendor; Provider will assess and must approve in accordance with security standards; Provider reserves right to object and provide reasonable alternatives."

- Analytics export: security supports the product sketch but insists on: (a) no export of raw prompts or embeddings; (b) retention <=30 days on Provider side; (c) BrightLeaf must attest annually that they will not use the exported metrics for model training; and (d) we should include an audit right (on-site or portal) limited to telemetry handling practices.

If Legal wants to accept a tighter set of commitments (attestations + audit), I can sign off once the vendor evidence is uploaded.

Karthik
Security Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: BrightLeaf DPA: subprocessor & analytics export language — Product/Security review

Thanks — I chatted with Jamie/Alison this morning. They pushed back on audit rights being too heavy but are okay with an annual attestation and a requirement to upload LogSight's SOC2 report to our vendor portal. They also accepted limiting exports to aggregated metrics and a 30-day retention, provided the language is explicit.

Attached is a suggest redline doc with combined language from Product + Security: BL_DPA_final_suggested_language_20270520.docx (docx, 18 KB). Key points in the redline:
- Export limited to aggregated metrics; expressly prohibits raw prompts/embeddings/identifiers.
- Provider to maintain telemetry <=30 days.
- Customer may request addition of a named monitoring subprocessor (LogSight); Provider retains approval right and 30-day objection window.
- Customer to upload SOC2 for any named subprocessor to Redwood vendor portal within 5 business days of request; failure to provide will require Provider to proxy telemetry or deny the subproc.
- Customer attestation (annual) that exported metrics will not be used for model training.

Requesting final accept/decline so I can push this back to BrightLeaf. If Product + Security both sign off, Legal will run the final clean redline and then we can get counter-signature.

Marcus

I reviewed the suggested redline. Product signs off on the language Marcus proposed with two small edits: (1) change retention wording to "Provider shall not retain telemetry longer than 30 days from collection, except as required by law"; (2) add a clause that exported metrics must be further aggregated across a minimum of X customers or Y sessions (we can use X=3 / Y=500) to reduce re-identification risk.

Karthik: if you can confirm the SOC2 upload + attestation approach satisfies Security, we can tell BrightLeaf we approve and get Legal to prepare the final DPA.

Olga
